extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, applicants, registered patent attorneys/agents, and other USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for appointing, acting as, revoking, and withdrawing patent practitioners or other representatives before the USPTO (power of attorney, acting in representative capacity, certifications, limited recognition, correspondence address/Customer Number practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO cannot aid in selection of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States Patent and Trademark Office cannot aid in the selection of a patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may suggest employing a registered patent attorney or agent if patentable subject matter appears and applicant seems unfamiliar with proper prosecution; use form paragraph 4.10 when suggesting use of attorney/agent. Examiner should not suggest employment of an attorney/agent if the application appears to contain no patentable subject matter. Listing of registered practitioners available on USPTO website and via OED/Inventors Assistance Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney must: (1) be in writing; (2) name one or more representatives in compliance with paragraph (c); (3) give the representative power to act on behalf of the principal; and (4) be signed by the applicant for patent (§ 1.41(b)) or the assignee of the entire interest of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.32(b). Form PTO/SB/81 may be used. Principal means applicant or assignee of entire interest; power must identify representatives in the manner required by 1.32(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be named as representative
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney may only name as representative: (1) one or more joint inventors (§ 1.45); (2) those registered patent practitioners associated with a Customer Number; or (3) ten or fewer patent practitioners, stating the name and registration number of each patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.32(c). Firms are not recognized. If more than ten practitioners are named, the power of attorney must be accompanied by a separate paper indicating which ten are to be recognized. If a name does not match the registration number, the Office recognizes the person associated with the registration number (Office enters registration number, not name).

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number practice and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A Customer Number may be used to designate correspondence address, fee address, and to submit a list of patent practitioners such that those practitioners associated with the Customer Number would have power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designating practitioners via Customer Number makes the practitioners associated therewith recognized for correspondence and power of attorney purposes (see MPEP § 403). A power of attorney to practitioners associated with a Customer Number will be treated as a request to revoke any prior powers of attorney previously given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner registration requirement and suspended/disbarred practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: For a power of attorney to be valid, the attorney or agent appointed must be registered to practice before the USPTO in accordance with 37 CFR 11.6. Any power of attorney given to a practitioner who has been suspended or disbarred by the Office is ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/81 may be used. If a named representative is not registered, use form paragraph 4.09 to notify applicant and change correspondence address to the first named inventor unless otherwise instructed. If uncertain about recognition status, PALM inquiry and contact OED are advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting in a representative capacity — signature and registration number requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent practitioner acting in a representative capacity appears in person or signs a paper in practice before the USPTO in a patent case, his or her personal appearance or signature constitutes a representation that he or she is authorized to represent the party, and the paper must set forth the practitioner's registration number, name and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.34. Papers filed by a registered practitioner not of record must include name and registration number. Acceptance of such papers is to facilitate replies and avoid filing powers in individual applications when firm composition changes. Further proof of authority may be required. A person acting in a representative capacity may NOT sign certain documents (power of attorney, change of correspondence address except limited situations, terminal disclaimer, request for express abandonment without continuing application, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregistered attorney or agent appointment is void
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointment of an attorney or agent who is neither registered to practice before the USPTO nor one of the named inventors is void ab initio and will not be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 4.09 to notify applicant. All correspondence must be signed by named applicants/owners or a duly appointed registered attorney/agent. If the named representative is unregistered, the Office will send official filings/correspondence to the first named inventor and will not add the unregistered individual to the practitioner-of-record list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition exceptions (non-registered individuals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual not registered may, upon showing circumstances making it necessary or justifiable and of good moral character, be given limited recognition by the OED Director to prosecute specified patent application(s); certain nonimmigrant aliens and persons for international applications may receive limited recognition under specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 11.9. Limited recognition does not extend beyond the specified application(s) and is not granted while examinees await registration. For international (PCT) practice, an individual not registered may prosecute before certain international authorities if entitled to practice before the national office with which the international application is filed (see PCT Art.49, Rule 90, §1.455).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate power of attorney practice eliminated
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective June 25, 2004, the associate power of attorney practice has been eliminated and the Office no longer accepts a power of attorney signed by a principal to name an associate power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any appointment of an associate power of attorney filed on or after June 25, 2004 will not be accepted; see MPEP § 406 for related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of power of attorney — who and how
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney may be revoked at any stage by the applicant for patent or an assignee of the entire interest or the owner of the entire interest of a patent; revocation of a power given to practitioners associated with a Customer Number will revoke prior powers; fewer than all applicants/assignees may revoke only for sufficient cause and payment of petition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.36(a). Revocation is effective on the date received by the Office (not date of acceptance). A patent practitioner will be notified of revocation and notice is mailed to the correspondence address in effect before revocation. Form PTO/SB/82 may be used to revoke or change power of attorney. An assignment alone does not automatically operate as revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney or agent of record — approval, timing and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent attorney or agent given power of attorney may withdraw as attorney or agent of record only upon application to and approval by the Director; withdrawal is effective when approved rather than when received, and the Director usually requires at least 30 days between approval of withdrawal and the later of the expiration date of a reply period or the last date obtainable by petition and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.36(b) and 10.40. When requesting withdrawal, practitioner should briefly state reasons; disciplinary rule 10.40(a) prohibits withdrawal until reasonable steps taken to avoid foreseeable prejudice to client. If withdrawal is based on client failure to compensate or other conduct, identify as 'irreconcilable differences' and submit supporting evidence as proprietary. Form PTO/SB/83 may be used. Deleting all practitioners associated with a Customer Number may be denied if reply due and insufficient time remains to file a reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee may revoke applicant's power and prosecute
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee of record of the entire interest can revoke the power of attorney of the applicant and appoint a new power of attorney, and assignees of entire interest may conduct prosecution to the exclusion of the inventive entity or prior assignees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 3.71. An assignee becomes of record by filing a statement in compliance with § 3.73(b) signed by an authorized party. Form PTO/SB/80 may be used by an assignee to revoke and appoint a new power of attorney. In applications accorded status under 37 CFR 1.47(a), assignee of entire interest of available inventors may revoke powers given by inventors who signed the declaration (see 1.32(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney naming more than ten practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided for joint inventors or Customer Number practice, the Office will not recognize more than ten patent practitioners as being of record in an application or patent; a power naming more than ten must be accompanied by a paper indicating which ten are to be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.32(c)(3). If power is not entered because more than ten were named, a copy should be refiled with the separate paper indicating the recognized ten. When Customer Number practice is used the Customer Number may designate practitioners without listing ten individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and signature obligations (37 CFR 10.18 / 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: By presenting any paper to the USPTO (signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating), the party certifies: (1) statements of own knowledge are true, statements on information and belief are believed to be true, and false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001; and (2) to the best of the party’s knowledge, information and belief, formed after reasonable inquiry, the paper is not for an improper purpose; claims/legal contentions are warranted by existing law or by nonfrivolous argument for change; factual contentions have evidentiary support or likely will after reasonable investigation; denials are warranted on the evidence or reasonably based on lack of information or belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 10.18(a)-(c) and related discussion. Violations may jeopardize validity/enforceability of application/patent and may lead to sanctions including holding facts established, returning papers, precluding filing/presentation, monetary sanctions, terminal disclaimers, or terminating proceedings. Practitioners may also face disciplinary action. The 'reasonable inquiry' standard tracks Fed. R. Civ. P. 11: reasonableness depends on time available and probability more investigation will uncover important evidence; does not create duty to perform a prior art search before filing an application. OED handles determinations of violations and possible practitioner discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of misleading or false statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of misleading or inaccurate statements of fact by applicants or false statements by practitioners during prosecution has resulted in patents being held unenforceable and other adverse outcomes, including disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases (e.g., Refac Int'l Ltd. v. Lotus Dev. Corp., Paragon Podiatry Lab. v. KLM Labs, General Electro Music Corp. v. Samick Music Corp.) illustrate that false/misleading statements can render patents unenforceable. Practitioners should advise clients that information provided must be reliable; OED will be involved when circumstances warrant determination of violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal from register for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 10.11, a letter may be sent to individuals on the register to ascertain whether they desire to remain; failure to reply within a specified time will result in removal from the register and publication in the Official Gazette; reinstatement may occur upon appropriate action and payment of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1702 for related practice. Removal is administrative and reinstatement requires payment of fee per §1.21(a)(3) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling for applications in interference
rubrics_metrics.description: While an application is involved in an interference, no power of attorney of any kind should be entered in such application by the technical support staff; any power of attorney or revocation received should be forwarded to the Service Branch of the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences because all parties must be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter power of attorney in interference files; forward received powers/revocations to the Board's Service Branch for notification of all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: International application representation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation in international (PCT) applications: applicants may be represented by attorneys or agents registered to practice before the USPTO; non-registered individuals may be granted limited recognition under narrow conditions; 37 CFR 1.455 governs representation in international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 11.9 and 37 CFR 1.455 and PCT provisions (Art.49, Rule 90, PCT Rules 83.1bis and 90.1). An appointment of a registered Canadian patent agent is valid only if given by applicants all located in Canada (37 CFR 11.6(c) context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro se applicant certifications and risks
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant acting pro se (representing themselves) makes the certifications under 37 CFR 10.18(b) when presenting papers and may be subject to sanctions under 37 CFR 10.18(c) for violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.31 and 1.4(d)(4). If patentable subject matter is disclosed and applicant is unfamiliar with prosecution, examiner may suggest employing a registered practitioner (form paragraph 4.10) but should not if no patentable subject matter.
